Requirement: 16 RGB LEDs, common anode = 48 dies on 8 GPIO lines. Each line is the anode of 2 RGB LEDs; their 6 cathodes sit on 6 of the other 7 lines. One resistor per line.
One die lit at a time, ~100 µs slots, 200 Hz frame, 8-bit PWM per slot, gamma and white balance in firmware. Constant current per die and a built-in power cap.
8 lines on port P1 (GPIOTE + timer scanning, high drive ~4 mA). Option: P2 extra drive (~14 mA) scanned by the RISC-V VPR. Stay under 15 mA total GPIO current.
Two LEDs in series must need more than VDD. With XL-1010RGB-YG red at 2.1 V: 4.2 V > 3.5 V. Avoid LEDs whose red Vf can drop below 1.8 V.
Copy the Nordic nRF54L15-QFAA reference circuit (config 1, DC/DC) and reference layout v0.8, including the RF matching network.
Chip antenna at the tree tip with a copper keep-out on both boards (no LEDs or copper under the top ~17 mm). Add pi-match pads; tune with a VNA if possible.
Open point: Chip antenna vs Nordic PCB antenna
